config.classes_note: Five classes, each sourced from the field by locus: the screener as a detector of paper-mill output (B2), as a research-integrity tool (B4), as post-publication assessment (B3), as a curator and corrector of the scholarly record (B3, B4), and as a detector of bogus or fraudulent publications (B2, B3, B4). No field source places the screener in a class of the archive's own; 'aggregators of machine-mediated reception work' is the MMRS record's class, an archive source, ledgered as MMRS claims and not run as an O-class here, since the brief confines classes to what B sources. The aliases are the entity's name, its abbreviation PPS (case-sensitive; it also names other things, and candidates on it are read and set aside where they do), its host, and its three makers' names. The detector terms (tortured phrase(s), SCIgen, Mathgen, Feet of Clay) were also grepped over data/texts before the pass and match nothing. Admission by reading (§3.4): a candidate is admitted when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim bearing on the screener, or applies an archive category to a class the field sources for it (paper-mill output, research integrity, post-publication assessment, the scholarly record's correction, bogus publications); a bare mention, a generic use of 'scientific literature' or 'scholarly record' about another object, or a list item is not a claim.
